currentContext.strengths: Engineering and execution capability trusted by major Indian steel producers (Tata Steel, Tata Steel Tinplate, JSW Steel Coated Products, JSW JFE Electrical Steel, ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India, Jindal Steel Odisha, Jindal India, Godawari Power & Ispat), evidenced by repeat and expanding order relationships.|Value Services (revamps, spares, services) provided consistent performance during a year of delayed large project decisions, reducing dependence on the new-project order cycle.|Order book grew approximately 74% year-on-year to INR 11,869 million as of December 2025 on order wins exceeding INR 8,600 million during the year, giving revenue visibility as orders move from engineering/mobilisation into execution.|Access to John Cockerill Group technology and brand (referral & technical royalty and brand-fee arrangements with parent John Cockerill SA), supporting technical credibility on complex commissioning work.|Ongoing consolidation of the Group's Metals business with India at its core is intended to unify technology, engineering, manufacturing and execution into one platform, positioning India as a base for both domestic and international projects.
currentContext.strategies: "Audacity under Control": pursuing ambitious growth while exercising discipline in project selection, favouring projects aligned to capabilities with stronger commercial structures over volume.|Tightened project governance, detailed review of cost structures, and simplified decision-making processes to build consistency in execution.|Advancing consolidation of the John Cockerill Group's Metals business with India at its core, unifying technology, engineering, manufacturing and execution into one platform and repositioning India as a base for both domestic and international projects.|Building Value Services (revamps, spares, services) into a structural pillar of future growth that is not dependent on the new-project order cycle.|For 2026: grow in the company's key regions and core technologies, convert the order book into revenue performance, strengthen Value Services, advance the Metals consolidation, and continue investing in R&D, technology, capability and people.|Strategic positioning built on brownfield optimisation over speculative greenfield risk, high-margin value services, decarbonisation technologies, automation and digital solutions, and lifecycle partnership models.|Disciplined capital allocation, operational efficiency, digitalisation, lifecycle service offerings and decarbonisation technologies to strengthen competitiveness and long-term value creation.|The Board recommends dividends annually for shareholder approval at the AGM; for the year ended December 31, 2025 it recommended a final dividend of INR 7.00 per equity share (70% of face value), to be tabled at the 40th AGM on June 25, 2026. Related-party dealings with parent John Cockerill SA (services, goods, brand/royalty fees, and a proposed indemnity for a Parent Company Guarantee to a Group fellow subsidiary) are governed by the Company's Policy on Materiality of Related Party Transactions and conducted on an arm's-length, Transfer Pricing Guidelines basis, with Audit Committee/Board/Shareholder approvals sought as required.
currentContext.expansion: The Company's 'expansion' activity is execution of customer capex projects (equipment supply, erection and commissioning of steel-processing lines) rather than its own plant capacity build-out. During the year it progressed a multi-project portfolio: TATA-CAL (under Performance Guarantee completion), TATA-CGL1 (commissioning completed, under PG), TATA-CGL2 (commissioning completed February 2026), AMNS-CGL3 (commissioning completed, under PG), AMNS-CGAL (erection completed, under commissioning), JSOL-ARP1 (commissioned January 2025, FAC completed February 2025), JSOL-ARP2 (commissioning completed February 2026), JSOL-CGL2 (under commissioning), Jindal India-CCL3 (under erection), and BRS-CCL (FAC achieved). New orders secured during the year included a Continuous Galvanising Line revamp for Jindal India at Ranihati, tunnel furnaces for JSW JFE Electrical Steel at Nashik, a Cold Rolling Mill for Godawari Power and Ispat in Chhattisgarh, a Continuous Annealing Line/Push-Pull Pickling Line/Acid Regeneration Plant for Tata Steel Tinplate at Jamshedpur, and a Continuous Galvanising Line/Push-Pull Pickling Line/6-Hi Twin Stand mill for JSW Steel Coated Products at Khopoli. Strategic positioning favours brownfield optimisation over speculative greenfield risk, alongside decarbonisation technologies, automation/digital solutions and lifecycle partnership models. Industry-level capacity expansion (India's crude steel capacity, targeted to scale from an estimated 200 million tonnes in FY25 to 300 million tonnes by 2030 under the National Steel Policy, concentrated in Odisha and Chhattisgarh) is the demand backdrop for the Company's equipment and services business, not the Company's own capex.
currentContext.mdna: India's steel industry is expected to remain one of the strongest contributors to global steel demand growth in 2026, with domestic steel demand projected to grow in the mid- to high-single-digit range, supported by continued infrastructure investment and manufacturing expansion.|Sustained public capital expenditure in transport, urban development, renewable energy and industrial corridors is expected to support steel consumption growth; PLI-scheme-driven manufacturing growth is expected to add incremental demand.|Technology and equipment providers are expected to benefit from continued investment by steel producers in modernisation and sustainability.|Execution risk: delays in infrastructure projects, land acquisition challenges and fiscal constraints could slow the pace of steel offtake; moderation in public capex could soften near-term demand.|Raw material cost volatility, particularly dependence on imported coking coal, exposes the value chain to global supply disruption, geopolitical risk and currency fluctuation that could affect margins.|Trade risk: continued surplus steel exports from global markets may pressure domestic pricing even with safeguard measures in place.|Capacity-expansion risk: rapid commissioning of new capacity without commensurate demand growth could temporarily affect utilisation levels across the industry.|Tightening environmental and regulatory requirements are expected to necessitate higher capital investment in decarbonisation and energy efficiency, strengthening long-term competitiveness but raising short-term costs.|Company-level outlook: global overcapacity, export pressure from surplus regions, raw-material price volatility, currency fluctuation and tightening environmental regulation may continue to influence industry dynamics through 2026.|Order book at the end of December 2025 stood at INR 11,869 million, up 74% over the previous year, following order wins during the year exceeding INR 8,600 million.|A significant portion of these orders is in early stages (engineering, design, mobilisation) and is expected to translate into revenue over coming periods, providing visibility and continuity to performance.|During the year the Company secured significant orders from JSW JFE Electrical Steel Nashik Private Limited, Tata Steel Limited, Godawari Power & Ispat Limited, ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India and Jindal Steel Odisha Limited, spanning detailed engineering, equipment supply, erection and commissioning.

risks.note: Order inflows were lower than anticipated during the year, weighing on overall performance; revenue depends on the pace at which customers convert capex decisions into signed orders and orders progress from engineering/mobilisation into execution.

risks.risk: Global steel overcapacity and Chinese export pressure
risks.note: Continued weak global steel demand and excess supply, exemplified by record Chinese exports of around 119 million tonnes in 2025, may pressure domestic steel prices and constrain the investment appetite of the Company's Indian steel-producer customers.

risks.risk: Raw material price and currency volatility
risks.note: Volatility in raw material prices (particularly coking coal and alloying elements) and currency fluctuations could increase customers' production costs and affect margins, indirectly affecting demand for the Company's equipment and services.

risks.risk: Rising financing costs for capital-intensive customer projects
risks.note: Higher global interest rates raise financing costs for the capital-intensive steel-plant projects the Company supplies and executes, which can delay or dampen customer capex decisions.

Evolving regulatory and environmental standards may require significant capital investment by steel producers for compliance, an uncertainty that flows through to the timing and scale of orders for the Company.

Operational risks including project execution delays, infrastructure bottlenecks, and energy supply volatility could impact production schedules and profitability across the Company's project portfolio, which spans multiple concurrent commissioning, erection and PG-phase sites.
The Company's Risk Management Framework explicitly identifies cybersecurity as one of the major functional risk areas requiring proactive identification, assessment and mitigation.

The Managing Director (Michael Kotas) resigned effective July 31, 2025 amid Group role changes and was replaced by Frederic Martin via postal ballot; the Company Secretary (Haresh Vala) also resigned effective September 30, 2025 and was replaced in December 2025 — leadership transitions that carry continuity risk during a period of active order-book growth and Group restructuring.
